linkedin.title: Most news feeds treat you like a demographic, not a person.
linkedin.body:
We have all felt the frustration of a feed that shows us things we do not care about. The standard approach for most apps is to guess what you like based on what people similar to you have clicked. It is a logic built on broad assumptions rather than your actual interests.

At Headlinne, we built our recommendation engine differently. Instead of looking at groups, the system pays attention to the specific signals you give it. When you read an article to the end, or skip a topic entirely, the AI learns from those actions. It is not trying to predict your next click to keep you scrolling forever. It is trying to understand the specific subjects and perspectives that genuinely matter to you today.

This creates a feedback loop that gets smarter the more you use it. You are not a data point in a generic category. You are an individual with changing interests. Your news feed should reflect that.

slides.headline: SpaceX catches massive rocket booster mid-air
slides.subtitle: The Mechazilla tower successfully grabbed the descending booster

slides.explanation: The Starship booster is a massive piece of hardware. It stands taller than a 20-story building and is heavy enough to rival a small naval vessel.

slides.headline: This catch was not the first attempt
slides.explanation: SpaceX had previously aborted a planned catch for this specific flight before successfully executing the maneuver on this attempt.
Six independent news outlets verified the details of this event, confirming the successful catch after the initial abort.

slides.subtitle: Read the full story on Headlinne.

instagram.caption:
SpaceX just accomplished a major engineering milestone by catching a returning rocket booster with the giant mechanical arms

of its launch tower.  This maneuver, often called the chopstick catch, is designed to allow for rapid reuse of rocket hardware.

It marks a significant shift in how we think about landing spacecraft compared to traditional ocean splashdowns.

We tracked this story across six different news sources to ensure accuracy as reports came in. It is a complex process that requires extreme precision.
